convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load 'DSSBressert' custom indicator (not a built-in MT5 indicator) and includes external TradeAlgorithms.mqh library for order management. The custom indicator logic must be manually reimplemented in Python.

other_exits: Long position closed when DnValue > UpValue (sell signal triggers BUY_Close if BuyPosClose=true)
Short position closed when UpValue > DnValue (buy signal triggers SELL_Close if SellPosClose=true)

params.description: MM=-0.1 means 0.1 lots fixed; positive values mean deposit fraction

position_sizing.conditional_logic: If MM < 0, abs(MM) is used as fixed lot size; if MM > 0, it is the fraction of deposit

custom_logic_notes: DSSBressert is a Double Smoothed Stochastic by Walter Bressert. It applies EMA smoothing to a standard stochastic, producing two buffers: the smoothed stochastic (UpValue/buffer0) and its signal line (DnValue/buffer1). Entry requires crossover confirmation: the crossover must exist at SignalBar=1 (previous bar) AND the values at bar 0 must satisfy the additional condition (UpValue[0]<=DnValue[0] for buy, DnValue[0]<=UpValue[0] for sell), meaning the crossover just happened. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh library provides BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, GlobalVariableDel_, CIsNewBar, and LoadHistory helper functions. Permission flags (BuyPosOpen, SellPosOpen, BuyPosClose, SellPosClose) gate each action independently. Recount flag handles failed CopyBuffer calls by retrying on next tick.
python_conversion_notes: Must reimplement DSSBressert indicator: compute standard stochastic with period=13, then apply EMA smoothing with period=8 twice (once on raw stochastic, once on the result to get signal line). TradeAlgorithms.mqh functions need manual Python equivalents: position opening with SL/TP, position closing, and new-bar detection. The crossover logic uses bars [1] and [0] - bar[1] must show the dominant direction (Up>Dn for bullish, Dn>Up for bearish) while bar[0] must show the crossover just forming (Up<=Dn or Dn<=Up respectively). Lot sizing: if MM<0, use abs(MM) as fixed lots; if MM>0, use as deposit fraction. Default params: SL=1000 points, TP=2000 points, deviation=10 points.
